Chapter 4: Add/Edit Characters

This chapter introduces mutation by adding merge configuration, create behavior, and update behavior to the same boundary. The workflow expands from reading data to saving new and edited records through the service.

Keep mutation policy inside the pipeline and committed Feature State inside the service, while the component owns only local form, mode, and feedback state. That separation makes the add/edit flow extensible instead of ad hoc.

Choose merge semantics before implementing create.

Creating and editing look similar in a form, but they make different promises to the collection. A create must preserve the records already present; an edit must replace one known record without disturbing the others. This chapter makes that distinction explicit before the service begins sending mutation requests through the pipeline.

Why this boundary matters

owns the merge policy, so the service can express intent through mergeState() and replaceState() instead of rebuilding arrays by hand. That keeps collection updates immutable and predictable while the component remains focused on temporary editor state and user feedback.

Use this structure for

  • forms that create records without replacing the existing collection
  • edits that must update one record by identity
  • features where create and update need visibly different write paths

By the end of this chapter

You will have append-style merge behavior configured for new characters, service-owned create and update methods, and an editor that routes each operation through the correct pipeline API without moving Feature State ownership into the component.

Chapter 4 Starting Point and Change Map

Start with the completed Chapter 2 project. This chapter updates app.config.ts and example.service.ts, then adds domain/editor helpers and expands the component, template, and tests. The FeatureCell key, initial collection, and service ownership do not change.

Two Requests, Two Collection Promises
  • Create submits [C] through append-configured mergeState(): [A, B] → [A, B, C].
  • Update derives a complete replacement collection and submits it through replaceState(): [A, B] → [A, B′].
Local Tutorial Concurrency

The example reads the current in-memory collection, derives the next collection, and replaces it. In a server-backed or multi-writer feature, resolve concurrent writes with server authority, version checks, or a documented conflict policy instead of assuming the local snapshot is current.

Step 1: Configure Array Merge Behavior
↑ top

Before the service can add a new character correctly, the registered needs append-style merge semantics. The default merge path replaces the existing array with the incoming array. That is correct for full replacement updates, but it is wrong for this tutorial's create flow because createCharacter() submits one new character through mergeState() and expects that record to be appended to the existing collection.

To change that Merge-stage behavior, install the package and register withArrayAppendMergeBehavior in app.config.ts. This makes mergeState() concatenate the incoming one-item array with the current committed collection, which is the exact behavior needed when adding a new character without replacing the others.

Make the Change
  1. Install the package. 
    npm install @sdux-vault/addons
  2. Open app.config.ts
  3. Import withArrayAppendMergeBehavior from .
  4. Pass [withArrayAppendMergeBehavior] as the behavior list for provide(). 
    {{ appConfigFile().source }}
Why This Behavior Is Required
  • mergeState() is the right API for adding a new record to an existing collection.
  • Without array-append merge behavior, the incoming one-item array would replace the entire current collection.
  • With withArrayAppendMergeBehavior, that same one-item array is appended immutably to the committed collection.
  • This keeps add and edit distinct: create uses mergeState() to append, while update will use replaceState() to swap one existing character by identity.
Avoid Manual Array Merging

You could build the next collection manually with a spread expression such as [...currentCharacters, newCharacter], but that is the wrong approach for this tutorial.

The spread operator itself does not mutate the array. The anti-pattern is pushing merge policy into the service instead of configuring it in the pipeline. In , append behavior belongs to the Merge stage so mergeState() can apply that rule consistently instead of forcing application code to reimplement it by hand.

Step 2: Add the Add/Edit Service Slice
↑ top

This step turns the user-directed read example into the first mutation slice. Keep the same boundary: the service owns the , while the component owns only temporary editor state. What changes now is the write path. The service gains the create and update methods that mutate the registered collection, and a small domain helper keeps ID assignment and draft creation out of the Angular service body.

Assume the Angular form primitives are already familiar. Focus on the boundary: the service assigns IDs, routes creates through mergeState(), routes updates through replaceState(), and keeps every write inside the service instead of spreading mutation logic across the component and template.

Make the Change
  1. Add the example.character-domain.ts file to the project. 
    {{ characterDomainFile().source }}
  2. Update example.service.ts to add the createCharacter and updateCharacter methods. 
    {{ serviceFile().source }}
Supporting Domain File

The example.character-domain.ts maintains the draft type, next-ID helper, and character factory used by this add/edit slice.

This file is intentionally separate so the service stays minimal and the chapter stays focused on the state boundary instead of helper logic.

What to Look For
  • The service owns the write path just as completely as it owned the read path.
  • Create uses mergeState() because it appends a new record to the existing collection.
  • Update uses replaceState() because it replaces one existing record by identity.
  • The domain helper supports add/edit mechanics, but it does not own any behavior. The service still owns the .

The collection picker, detail panel, and form now all react to the same -managed collection.

This is the first full CRUD-style expansion that still keeps the tutorial disciplined. The component gains form state, mode state, and feedback state, but the service remains the only place that creates or replaces Feature State. Keep that same boundary in place: the service owns the , and the component owns only temporary UI state. The component does not call APIs directly, and it does not mutate the registered collection. The service remains the single source of truth for all Feature State. That is the boundary to preserve before a later destructive-action step adds deletion.

Keep this file separate so the component stays minimal and the chapter stays focused on the state boundary instead of helper logic.

Returned Object Is Not Commit Confirmation

In this example, updateCharacter(999, draft) constructs and returns the requested replacement object, but the replaceState() factory finds no matching record and commits an equivalent collection. It does not append the missing character. The returned replacement object proves only what was submitted; it does not prove that the update committed. The service spec verifies both the returned object and unchanged collection. Drive production success feedback from an authoritative operation result.

Add/Edit Outcome Contract
Add and edit requests, their FeatureCell APIs, and committed outcomes
Action FeatureCell request Expected result
Add a valid draft mergeState() Appends one character using the largest current ID plus one.
Edit a known ID replaceState() Replaces only the matching record and preserves all others.
Edit an unknown ID replaceState() Leaves the collection equivalent; it never becomes create.
Invalid form or Cancel No request Committed State remains unchanged.
What to Look For
  • The component now owns local editor state in addition to local selection state.
  • The template adds a form and feedback region, but it still does not call APIs directly.
  • Saving a new record and saving an edited record both flow through the same service-owned .
  • Delete is still intentionally absent so this slice can focus on non-destructive mutation only.
Step 4: Chapter Round-up
↑ top

The Add & Edit Characters chapter is complete once characters can be added and edited successfully.

Run and Verify
  1. Return to the running Angular application and verify that you can add a character, select it, edit it, and see the detail panel react to the saved State.
  2. Submit an invalid draft and confirm validation prevents a FeatureCell request. Cancel both create and edit modes and confirm committed State remains unchanged.
Chapter 4 Summary
  1. Create appends one identity; update replaces the matching identity without disturbing other records.
  2. Invalid or canceled work sends no FeatureCell request and leaves committed State unchanged.
  3. Save this checkpoint for Chapter 4, which adds explicit, confirmable deletion.
